timeline.title: A Short History of the Big Day
items: Ancient Rome
The flame veil
Roman brides wore a veil the colour of flame, called the flammeum, on their wedding day.
The white dress
Queen Victoria married Prince Albert in white, and brides around the world followed her lead.
Here comes the bride
A royal wedding in London used marches by Wagner and Mendelssohn. Couples have walked to them ever since.
Something borrowed
An old English rhyme gave brides a lucky list: something old, something new, borrowed and blue.
today: The newest chapter in the history of weddings. And, we think, the best one yet.

items: Let me not to the marriage of true minds admit impediments.
William Shakespeare, Sonnet 116

1 Corinthians 13

Kahlil Gibran, The Prophet, 1923

An old proverb
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: congratulations, {who}.

facts.title: Wedding Facts to Share at the Table
items: ring
Gold for good
Gold never rusts or tarnishes, which is one reason it became the metal of forever.
gift
Sweet confetti
In Italian, confetti are sugared almonds, the sweets once thrown and shared at celebrations.
eye
Happy tears
Scientists think tears of emotion differ from onion tears. So yes, wedding tears are the real thing.
moon
The honeymoon
A centuries old word: honey for the sweetness, moon for the month it was said to last.
cake
Five almonds
An old custom gives guests five sugared almonds: health, wealth, joy, children and long life.
star
Something blue
In wedding tradition, blue stands for loyalty and faithful love. A very good colour to wear.
facts.hand: Tradition explains a lot. It cannot explain how {who} found each other. We are just glad they did.

note.title: What we believe a marriage is
paras: We make a lot of magazines, and some of them stay with us. This was one of them.
We believe a marriage is not one big day but thousands of small ones: the coffee made for two, the coat held open, the choice to be a team, over and over again.
{who}, someone wanted you to have more than a card. They wanted pages full of you: your story, your faces, the moment the whole room cried.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, yours is the kind of love that makes everyone around you believe in it too.
